assertions.description: chrome.debugger is an extension API and is never exposed to web-page script — the process boundary the attach-time policy gate sits on.

On a managed Chrome 155+ browser where ExtensionSettings configures runtime_blocked_hosts for the extension, chrome.debugger.attach() rejects every target with the error "Host access is restricted by policy." — even targets listed in runtime_allowed_hosts.
assertions.test: Requires a managed profile with an ExtensionSettings policy plus an installed extension holding the debugger permission; call chrome.debugger.attach({tabId}, '1.3') from its service worker and inspect the rejection message. Not runnable from a web page.

assertions.description: When DisableScreenshots or a Data Loss Prevention rule restricts capture for the target, chrome.debugger.attach() rejects with "Screenshot capture is restricted by policy." at attach time.
assertions.test: Requires a managed profile with DisableScreenshots (or a DLP rule) plus an extension holding the debugger permission; the attach-time rejection carries the stable message. Not runnable from a web page.

assertions.description: The Chrome 155 enforcement is all-or-nothing: any configured runtime_blocked_hosts entry blocks attach() for all targets, deterministically at attach time, instead of individual CDP commands failing unpredictably mid-session.
assertions.test: Compare a pre-155 and a 155+ managed browser with the same ExtensionSettings policy: pre-155 attach() succeeds and later sendCommand calls fail per-command; 155+ attach() itself rejects. Extension-side behaviour, not observable from a web page.

assertions.description: Attachment is disclosed through trusted browser UI (the debugging infobar); no page-context property, event, or flag (including navigator.webdriver, which reflects WebDriver automation only) reveals a chrome.debugger attachment to the page.
